hadiths.arabicText: وَعَنْ مَالِك ، عَنْ أَبِي الزِّنَادِ ، أَنَّ عُمَرَ بْنَ عَبْدِ الْعَزِيزِ كَتَبَ إِلَى عَبْدِ الْحَمِيدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ زَيْدِ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ وَهُوَ عَامِلٌ عَلَى الْكُوفَةِ : أَنْ اقْضِ بِالْيَمِينِ مَعَ الشَّاهِدِ

hadiths.english_translation: Malik narrated to me that it reached him: That Abu Salamah ibn Abdul Rahman and Sulayman ibn Yasar were asked: 'Is judgment given with an oath along with a witness?' They said: 'Yes.' Malik said: 'The Sunnah has been established regarding judging with an oath along with a single witness, the claimant swears with his witness and establishes his right. If he refuses to swear, the defendant is made to swear. If he swears, that right falls from him. If he refuses to swear, the right is established against him for its owner.'

hadiths.english_translation: Chapter: Judgment regarding one who dies having a debt owed to him and a debt owed by him for which there is one witness.
hadiths.arabicText: بَابُ الْقَضَاءِ فِيمَنْ هَلَكَ ، وَلَهُ دَيْنٌ ، وَعَلَيْهِ دَيْنٌ لَهُ فِيهِ شَاهِدٌ وَاحِدٌ

hadiths.english_translation: Yahya said: Malik said regarding a man who dies having a debt owed to him with one witness, and a debt owed by him to people with one witness for them, and his heirs refuse to swear on their rights with their witness: He said: 'The creditors swear and take their rights. If anything remains, the heirs have no share of it, because the oaths were offered to them before and they abandoned them. Unless they say: We did not know our companion had surplus, and it is known that they only abandoned the oaths because of that, then I see that they should swear and take what remains after his debt.'

hadiths.arabicText: قَالَ يَحْيَى : قَالَ مَالِك ، فِي الرَّجُلِ يَهْلِكُ وَلَهُ دَيْنٌ عَلَيْهِ شَاهِدٌ وَاحِدٌ ، وَعَلَيْهِ دَيْنٌ لِلنَّاسِ لَهُمْ فِيهِ شَاهِدٌ وَاحِدٌ...

hadiths.english_translation: Yahya said: Malik said, from Jamil ibn Abdul Rahman al-Mu'adhdhin: That he used to attend Umar ibn Abdul Aziz while he was judging between people. When a man came to him claiming a right against another man, he would examine the case. If there was mixing or association between them, he would make the one claimed against swear an oath. If there was none of that, he would not make him swear. Malik said: 'This is our practice, that whoever claims against a man, the case is examined. If there is mixing or association between them, the defendant is made to swear. If he swears, that right falls from him. If he refuses to swear and returns the oath to the claimant, and the claimant swears, he takes his right.'

hadiths.english_translation: Chapter: Judgment Regarding the Testimony of Children.

Yahya said: Malik said, from Hisham ibn Urwah: That Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr used to judge with the testimony of children among themselves regarding wounds. Malik said: 'The established practice among us is that the testimony of children is acceptable among themselves regarding wounds, and is not acceptable against others. Their testimony among themselves is only acceptable regarding wounds alone, not in other matters, if this is before they separate, or are coached, or are taught. If they separate, there is no testimony for them unless they had reliable witnesses testify to their testimony before they separated.'

hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Abu Umamah: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Whoever usurps the right of a Muslim man by his oath, Allah has forbidden Paradise for him and made the Fire obligatory for him.' They said: 'Even if it is something trivial, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Even if it is a twig from an arak tree, even if it is a twig from an arak tree, even if it is a twig from an arak tree.' He said it three times.

hadiths.english_translation: Yahya said: Malik said, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, that he heard Abu Ghatafan ibn Tarif al-Murri saying: 'Zayd ibn Thabit al-Ansari and Ibn Muti' disputed about a house between them before Marwan ibn al-Hakam while he was the governor of Madinah. Marwan ruled that Zayd ibn Thabit should swear on the pulpit. Zayd ibn Thabit said: I will swear to him in my place. Marwan said: No, by Allah, except at the place where rights are cut off. Zayd ibn Thabit kept swearing that his right was true, and refused to swear on the pulpit. Marwan ibn al-Hakam was amazed by that.' Malik said: 'I do not see that anyone should be made to swear on the pulpit for less than a quarter dinar, which is three dirhams.'
